A controller with significant interest holds more than 25% of the total number of issued shares (excluding treasury shares) or more than 25% of the total voting power in the company.

A person qualifies as a registrable controller if they hold or have the right to exercise significant influence or control over the company (for example, the right to appoint or remove directors holding a majority of board seats).
The company must enter the particulars into, or update, the Register of Registrable Controllers within 2 business days after receiving the information.
The company must give notice to each of its shareholders or members to find out whether that person is a registrable controller or knows the identity of one.
Failure to maintain the register is an offence under the Companies Act; ACRA may offer a composition sum in lieu of prosecution, and in serious cases the company can be struck off the register.

A nominee is generally not the registrable controller; the nominator (the person who gave the directions or on whose behalf the rights are exercised) is treated as holding the interest or control and is the registrable controller.
